title: Adding with apples
examples: Teacher, if I have two apples and you give me one more, how many do I have?
What does it mean to put apples together when we count?

explain.say: Today you will learn to add. Adding means putting groups together.
You have three apples. You get one more apple. Now you have four apples.
Altogether means all of them. Count every apple to find how many.
Start with four apples. Add two more apples. Count them all. You have six apples.
You can add other things too. Put your toys together and count them.
Count both groups. Touch each apple as you count it. Then you miss none.

faq.q: What does 'putting together' mean when we count?
faq.a: It means joining two or more groups of things into one big group. You count everything in that one group.
asks: What does it mean to add apples?
How do I count things together?

faq.q: If I have two apples and three more, how many altogether?
faq.a: You count them all: one, two, three, four, five. You have five apples altogether.

faq.q: Do I count the first group or the second group?
faq.a: You must count all the apples from both groups. We count them all to find the total.
asks: Do I just count the first pile?

faq.q: Can I use fingers to help me count?
faq.a: Yes. Fingers are a good way to count. Hold up one finger for each apple.
asks: Can I use my hands to count?

faq.q: What if the apples are not all the same size?
faq.a: It does not matter if they are different sizes. We count them by how many there are, not how big they look.

facts: We use counting to find the total amount.
The total is how many altogether.

quiz.say: Look at the apples. Count them all. How many apples altogether?
quiz.why: Two apples and one more apple make three apples.

wrong.1: Two is only the first group, so count the extra apple too.
wrong.2: Four is one too many, so count each apple only once.

quiz.say: Count the apples in both groups. How many apples altogether?
quiz.why: Three apples and two apples make five apples.

wrong.0: Six is one too many, so touch each apple once as you count.
wrong.1: Three is only the first group, so count the second group too.

quiz.say: Look at the sum. What is four add one?
quiz.why: Start at four and count on one more. That makes five.

wrong.0: Four is the first number, so count on one more.
wrong.2: Six is two more than four, but you add only one.
